- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7ffc57846a97afde24fbfc59b6b05d7562ef4df0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d6549239c0215eadcc3b12b24132999ee08e9636` — the merge of head `6f7999761865fa5f3ac88887a85323ea1b8c41d1` into base `7ffc57846a97afde24fbfc59b6b05d7562ef4df0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d6549239c0215eadcc3b12b24132999ee08e9636 && git checkout d6549239c0215eadcc3b12b24132999ee08e9636
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7ffc57846a97afde24fbfc59b6b05d7562ef4df0 6f7999761865fa5f3ac88887a85323ea1b8c41d1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7ffc57846a97afde24fbfc59b6b05d7562ef4df0 && git merge --no-ff 6f7999761865fa5f3ac88887a85323ea1b8c41d1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7ffc57846a97afde24fbfc59b6b05d7562ef4df0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7ffc57846a97afde24fbfc59b6b05d7562ef4df0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6f7999761865fa5f3ac88887a85323ea1b8c41d1`
Local-runs: none

PR #23565 (closes #23406). The head is the one the brief named and has not moved. Merge base `086fa4640f`. `origin/main` is now `7ffc57846a`, two commits on. Its only overlap is `protocol.ts`, in hunks near lines 5379 and 30295, far from this diff's hunks (17805, 19059, 21861, 22035, 23127). Inputs read: #23406's body, comments 6162860643, 6180799970 and 6181706743, the PR body, the net diff `origin/main...refs/review/pr-23565`, the three spec describes on `origin/main`, and the head's check-runs.

**Gates: the head's check-runs, read 2026-10-15T01:11Z.** 40 runs: 34 `success` and 6 `skipped`. None failed and none is still running.
- Test Core (1/6 to 6/6, and the aggregate) and Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger) were still running at the first read. All of them completed `success`.
- The skipped runs are the opt-in or path-filtered ones: Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix shard), Packed-tarball smoke, and Temporal Conformance.

### ① Derived judgments

**The remedy judgement: sound, and within the triage scope.**
- The diff makes `sealedWrite` `create` only when `parentVersion === null && mode !== 'draft'`. That reads `mode` the way `saveMetaItem` normalises it a few lines later (`request.mode === 'draft' ? 'draft' : 'publish'`), so an absent `mode` is a publish. The unit file pins both spellings of a publish: the unchanged `[#22591]` block sends no `mode`, and the new block sends `mode: 'publish'`.
- This matches the spec. `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema.parentVersion` says a present null asserts "no current row of this lifecycle". On a draft save that is the draft row, and it says nothing about the name. Triage 6162860643 set the scope the same way: "A first draft over an existing item gets the item's own remedy", "plus a true create as control".
- The dev's deviation on A2 holds; I verified it in the code.
  - `isSealedManagedItem` is `isArtifactBacked(type, name) && !registryAllowsOverlay(type)` (head `protocol.ts:17152`). The package door throws only under it.
  - The flow rule reaches `packagedBaseRefusal` only when `packagedArtifactOwner` is defined, and then the same predicate.
  - So "a row exists under the name" is constant-true wherever `sealedWrite` is read.
  - The only producer of `operation: 'create'` is `sealedWrite`. A grep of non-test sources finds no other caller: `automation.ts:1551` types its operation `'save' | 'delete'`, and the position write-through is retired (`.changeset/pre/15204-7b-position-write-through-retired.md`).
  - So A2 as written would have left the create remedy with no producer at any door, and the triage control could not have been pinned.
- **A draft pin over a name nothing holds:** no misclassification can be seen. `sealedWrite` has three references (head lines 21900, 21908, 22073), and both readers use it only inside the sealed predicate. Creating a free name is judged by the `allowRuntimeCreate` and ADR-0070 D1 gates, which do not read it.
- **The package door and the flow rule:** both read one value, computed once. For a flow, the rule spreads `operation` only when it is `create`, and `packagedBaseRefusal` falls back to `save`, so the two doors cannot disagree. The unit pin covers `flow`, `position` and `object` on both kernels.
- **The mirror case (accepted, noted):** a client creating its own item in draft mode under a held name now reads the edit sentence. That sentence still says "provided by a managed package and is sealed", so the client learns the name is held. The harm is asymmetric:
  - Following the edit remedy, such a client cannot act on another package's source.
  - Following the create remedy, as before this PR, an editor writes a duplicate.
  - The lifecycle reading therefore errs on the less harmful side.
  - Whether a first-party new-item flow (Studio, objectui#11773) pins a draft over a held name is NOT MEASURED.

**The open question: A.**
- **A leaves one client misdirected, reachable, but the gap is older than this PR.**
  - `GetMetaItemResponseSchema.version` serves `null` for an item served from a package artifact, and says "the next save creates one: pin it with `If-None-Match: *`".
  - That holds on the uncached read arms: `enableCache: false`, and the uncached reads at `rest-server.ts:6746`. The OCC test shows `version: null` for a code-registered item there. The default cached arm serves no `version`, and absence means "not published here", so no pin follows from it.
  - A spec-following editor that pins a publish-mode save that way reads the create remedy ("choose a name no package or built-in holds"). That is #23406's harm on the live-row side.
  - It is not a regression: it is the `[#22591]` reading and the card's own control, and the accept set is identical (403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` either way).
  - A mitigation: the same read publishes the protection envelope (`editable: false`).
- **B is not a Clause-② change by itself**, because it changes only the sentence. But it orphans the create remedy, which the triage scope ("a true create as control") and the `[#22591]` ruling both keep. A complete B needs a declared create (a request member or a create route). That is a new accepted key, which is a Clause-② yes. B is therefore beyond this card.
- **Ruling: A** for this PR. The publish-side residual needs its own card (see ③).

**The 409 sentence: holds.**
- `metadataConflictRefusal` sets `code`, `status`, `actualHead`, `currentVersion` and `expectedParent` in unchanged lines. The diff changes only the `conflict.message` ternary.
- The new arm requires `firstWritePin !== undefined && expected === null`. `saveConflict` passes `firstWritePin` only for `request.parentVersion === null`.
- The audit row (`recordOptimisticConflictAudit`, its note built from `err.*` at line 19136) is untouched, so `plugin-audit`'s `CONFLICT_NOTE` regex is unaffected.
- The other three `metadataConflictRefusal` callers (lines 24439, 28541, 29368) pass three arguments and are unchanged.
- The token path (`InboundVersionConflictError`) returns before the ternary.
- No code is minted: the diff touches no `packages/spec` file and no ledger, and the only code literals it adds are test assertions of `METADATA_CONFLICT` and `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`.
- The sentence still names the item and `(current is VERSION)`. Its remedy repeats `MetadataConflictErrorSchema.currentVersion`'s ("Send it as If-Match … or re-read the item to merge first"). The spec says the `error` text is never to be parsed.
- **Consumers of the old text.** I grepped the repo at the head for "since you loaded it" and "Expected parent". None of the matches is on the first-write-pin path:
  - the CLI delete tests (delete door);
  - `protocol.stored-migration.test.ts:655` (`storedParentVersion`, with `parentVersion` absent, so the old arm);
  - synthetic errors in `error-response-structured-arm-door-parity.test.ts` and `meta-item-response-shapes.test.ts`;
  - the OCC two-readers case (the token path).

  The one test on the path is the OCC `If-None-Match: *` case, which this PR updates. CHANGELOG and changeset quotes are history. No doc quotes the sentence.
- **Message length.** The fixed part is 291 characters with a 76-character keyed token, plus `TYPE/NAME`. A name of up to about 200 characters stays under REST's 500-character `truncateClientMessage` bound. The name-length bound is NOT MEASURED.

**The accept set does not move. Proof from the diff:**
1. `sealedWrite` flows only into `operation`, and `operation` is read only by `managedItemSealedSentence`, in both the package door and the flow rule. The verdict predicate (`isSealedManagedItem`), the `ITEM_LOCKED` named-base limb and `isPackagedBaseRefusal`, which reads `status` and `code` only, do not read it. Code 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` is set on unchanged lines.
2. The 409 change is message-only, on a path that already throws.
3. `saveConflict` widens its parameter type and adds one argument, and its audit row is unchanged.
4. The rest of the protocol.ts diff is comments.

**Pins.**
- Pins exist on both kernels, by construction:
  - REST: `rest-meta-sealed-first-draft-remedy.test.ts`, with `environmentId` undefined and `env_1`, through the real `RestServer` PUT route;
  - unit: the new `[#23406]` block, 2 kernels × 3 types = 6 tests;
  - the 409 pins: in `protocol.served-content-hash.test.ts` (draft and active) and the OCC case at the REST door.
- Ablation evidence is the dev's (6181706743), re-derived by reading:
  - Restoring `parentVersion === null ? 'create' : 'save'` makes `heldNameSentence` (which contains `GET /api/v1/meta/object`) the first draft's, so `remedyKind` reads `new-name`. All 6 new unit cases go red, consistent with the reported "6 failed, 13 passed": 16 cases in this file plus the 3 of the then-file `protocol.first-write-pin-conflict.test.ts` at `cb609acdd8`. The REST pin goes red on both kernels.
  - An unreachable `firstWritePin` falls back to "since you loaded it" and goes red.
  - `protocol.ts` and `packages/rest` are identical between `cb609acdd8` and the head, so the ablations at `cb609acdd8` apply to the head's fix.
- **The remedy control is real.** A publish-mode pin must read `new-name` in both files, so an over-fix such as B, or `save` always, turns it red.
- **The 409 control is weak (minor).** Its stale-token case returns at the `InboundVersionConflictError` branch, before the changed ternary. No pin covers an unpinned save that loses a first-write race (`expected === null`, `firstWritePin` undefined), which should keep the old sentence. The code is right by reading. Not blocking.
- **The engine-double ledger is untouched.** The diff touches no `scripts/` file, so `engine-double-contract.*.json` is unchanged. The gate's step runs in the `Lint · ESLint` job, which succeeded. The REST pin's `findOne` double, which answers null, is within that gate's verdict.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` for `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is correct under WHICH LEVEL (`pr-automation.yml:754`): no exported symbol and no accepted key or value is added. `firstWritePin` is a parameter of a private method, and `saveConflict` is private.
- `packages/rest` changes in test files only, so no published source moves there and no level is owed.
- `Clause-②: no` holds: the 409 body keeps `error`, `code` and `currentVersion` with the same types, and only the human sentence changes. The `check-changeset-no-major` level axis stands down on a `no` declaration.
- `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation A2 (constant-true): answered.** Sound, and verified in ①.
- **Deviation A4 (the true create pinned as a publish-mode PUT): answered.** It is the only producer of `create`. Sound.
- **Deviation: the conflict pin moved into the existing `served-content-hash` double: answered.** The ledger is untouched.
- **Deviation: the trailer pair and zero label writes:** process only, no contract effect.
- **The open question (publish-mode boundary): answered A; the residual is escalated.**
  - A spec-following editor that pins a publish save from `version: null` over a sealed item reads the create remedy. It is reachable on the uncached read arms and predates this PR.
  - The dev report names "the domain:engine seat" as carrier, but no card exists, and the PR body says "No one is assigned".
  - The seat should file a card: the remedy for a publish-mode first write over a package-artifact item, which needs a declared create fact (Clause-② yes) or a ruling that accepts the gap.
- **Out of scope: the stale `## create` docblock: escalated.**
  - Head `protocol.ts:17405` ("(Setup's position write-through does)") names a retired module, and since this PR it also omits the `/meta` publish first-write pin, the only remaining producer.
  - This PR rewrote the neighbouring `[#22591]` comments but not this one.
  - "The next PR that touches that docblock" is no carrier. A one-line fix-up here, or a named carrier.
- **New, out of scope: a clone race reads the REST door's remedy.**
  - `permission-set-clone.ts` calls `saveMetaItem` with `parentVersion: null` (publish). Its race-only `409 METADATA_CONFLICT`, after the catalog check, now reads "…(the first-write pin, If-None-Match: * on the REST door)… Send that version as If-Match to save over it…".
  - The clone door takes no `If-Match`.
  - The old sentence ("modified since you loaded it") was no better, the reach is low (a race only), and the clone test stubs `saveError`. Note for the seat; not blocking.
- **NOT MEASURED:**
  - every local run (read-only review);
  - the dev's test counts, ablations and 65-gate reconciliation, which I took from 6181706743 and did not re-run;
  - the runtime dispatcher's `/meta` PUT door (the same `metaSaveRequestOptions` and `saveMetaItem`, but not pinned);
  - objectui consumers of the 409 text;
  - whether a first-party new-item flow pins a draft over a held name;
  - the metadata-name length bound against the 500-character message cap;
  - a ConflictError with both sides null.

**Seat adoption** (2026-10-15T01:13Z). Adopted after an audit of the reviewer transcript: its writes are this record and a polling script under the brief's directory; 62 Bash calls, all reads (`git show`, `git diff`, REST GETs); one Monitor polling the check-runs; no MCP call, no GitHub write, no worktree, build or test run. The seat re-ran the landing prechecks on `6f79997618`:
- `ci-failure.mjs` exits 0;
- `check-governed-merges.mjs` reports no governed path and 333 lines;
- `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` exits 0;
- the only closing keyword is `Fixes #23406`, matching the claim 6180799970.

The seat rules:
- **The open question → A**, the dev's recommendation and this record's answer. Only a draft-lifecycle first-write pin reads as an edit, and a publish-mode first write keeps the create remedy, the triage scope's control. B needs a declared create fact, which is a contract change beyond `Clause-②: no`.
- **Findings 1 to 3** (the publish-side gap, the stale `## create` docblock, the clone door's lost-race 409) are filed as one card, #23577, for triage. None blocks this merge.

所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

  ```

    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/plugin-auth:test: Error: Test timed out in 10000ms.
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
